open_obligations: Note that the question-distribution part of the limitation is not addressed, since the tree is fixed.
Check that RL beating BC holds on full-book evaluation, not only on subtasks.
Confirm that Wu et al.'s reward models are trained on human comparisons at each node, not on whole-book judgements.
in.other_title: RL beats behavioral cloning at 175B; first-subtree training generalizes to full tree
in.rationale: Christiano et al. note X is trained by supervised learning from Amplify_H(X), whereas important applications would likely learn a reward function and train with RL. Wu et al. train recursive summarisation policies with reward modeling and RL and report 175B RL policies significantly outperform the behavioural-cloning baseline, with a smaller gain at 6B; their decomposition tree is fixed by an algorithm, not chosen by a human or model.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether recursive decomposition can be trained with learned rewards and RL rather than supervised learning, for GPT-3 book summarisation

text: The authors note X is trained by supervised learning from Amplify_H(X), whereas many important applications would likely learn a reward function from it and train X with RL. They also state the question distribution D must be broad enough to cover all subquestions asked during amplification, and that in the experiments D was usable directly whereas realistically the designer would have to construct it.
title: Question distribution must cover all subquestions; supervised rather than reward learning
